NOTE: the HIGH-1 regression fixture, and the most important file in this suite.
The engine is SATURATED, not deadlocked. The monitor's owner is pool-1-thread-3,
which is RUNNABLE inside a legitimate long call (a GAP-140 coverage walk runs ~20
minutes) and therefore OCCUPIES a pool slot — so only the other 7 of 8 threads can
ever block. A real wedge cannot look like this: GAP-137's dump had the owner
(HTTP-Dispatcher) OUTSIDE the pool, which is exactly why all 8 could block there.

KILLS: every majority threshold, including the shipped `blocked >= 6 (of 8)` and any
`>= N` for N <= 7. Each of those reads this healthy, progressing engine as wedged and
restarts it — reproduced against a real JVM. Only `blocked == seen` survives.
ALSO KILLS dropping the `^` anchor from the thread-header match: the indented
`owned by "pool-1-thread-3"` lines below would then be counted as thread headers.
